context.title: Samaria and an Ethiopian
context.summary: Persecution scatters the believers. Philip preaches in Samaria, where Simon the sorcerer is rebuked for trying to buy the Spirit's power. Then Philip explains Isaiah 53 to an Ethiopian official, who is baptized.
context.background: Jews and Samaritans had been divided for centuries, so Samaritans receiving the word (v. 14) is a major step. The Ethiopian came from the kingdom of Kush (in today's Sudan), and had traveled far to worship in Jerusalem.

customs.note: A royal title for the queen of Kush, not a personal name, much as 'Pharaoh' was a title.
Court officials were often eunuchs. The law barred eunuchs from the assembly (Deuteronomy 23:1), but Isaiah 56 promised them a place among God's people.

watchFor: Peter and John lay hands on the Samaritans, who receive the Spirit (v. 17).
The Ethiopian is reading aloud, as ancient readers usually did (v. 30).
'See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?' (v. 36).

people.name: Paul
people.summary: Saul was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name.

people.name: Stephen
people.summary: One of the seven deacons, who became a preacher of the gospel. He was the first Christian martyr. His personal character and history are recorded in Acts 6.

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Philip
people.summary: One of the “seven” (Acts 6:5), called also “the evangelist” (21:8, 9). He was one of those who were “scattered abroad” by the persecution that arose on the death of Stephen.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture.

people.name: John
people.summary: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Candace
people.summary: The queen of the Ethiopians whose “eunuch” or chamberlain was converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27).

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Gaza
places.summary: Called also Azzah, which is its Hebrew name (Deut. 2:23; 1 Kings 4:24; Jer. 25:20), strong, a city on the Mediterranean shore, remarkable for its early importance as the chief centre of a great commercial traffic with Egypt.

places.name: Azotus
places.summary: The Grecized form (Acts 8:40, etc.) of Ashdod.

places.name: Caesarea
places.summary: (Palestinae), a city on the shore of the Mediterranean, on the great road from Tyre to Egypt, about 70 miles northwest of Jerusalem, at the northern extremity of the plain of Sharon.

events.title: Saul persecutes the church
events.summary: Passage: Acts 8:1–3. People: Paul, Stephen. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: Philip preaches in Samaria
events.summary: Passage: Acts 8:4–25. People: Holy Spirit, John, Simon, Philip. Place: Samaria.

events.title: Conversion of Ethiopian Eunuch
events.summary: Passage: Acts 8:26–40. People: Holy Spirit, Candace, Philip. Place: Gaza.
